Thanks for the summary  that matches our notes. A few clarifications we need before scheduling the technical deep-dive: 

1) For region pinning: we need strong guarantees that both inference compute and any persisted artifacts (KV cache, snapshots, backups) will be stored only in the US region. Does Redwood support an enforcement mode that blocks any attempted replication to regions outside a pinned set?

2) Cross-region failover: our policy prefers failover within the same country where possible. Can you confirm if failover can be limited to US-only regions (warm standby) rather than triggering an EU/APAC failover?

3) Backups & retention: do you offer a US-only backup lifecycle, and can we set retention windows per-tenant (required for legal hold & deletion workflows)?

4) Logging & PII: What fields are logged by default for requests and responses? We need the option to redact or avoid storing the actual user input/response payloads and only retain request metadata and observability signals.

If you can send a short note addressing the four points above and any relevant attachments, we can evaluate and then book the tech session.

Hi Priya 

Thanks for the clear questions. Short answers below and a pointer to the attached matrix (cross-region-failover-matrix.xlsx) for the detailed behaviors. Longer notes follow each bullet.

1) Enforcement of region pinning: Yes. Redwood supports explicit region pinning at the tenant level. When a tenant is pinned to a region set (e.g., US-east + US-west), the control plane and runtime enforce routing such that inference requests, model artifacts, and persistent caches/backups are kept within the pinned region set. We have an enforcement mode that blocks automatic replication to regions outside the set and will raise an alarm and reject operations that would violate the policy.

2) Cross-region failover constrained to country/region: We support configurable failover policies. You can select strict "country-only" failover which prefers warm-standby nodes in the same country (US) and will only escalate to cross-region (EU/APAC) under explicit, pre-approved emergency conditions. That mode preserves RPOs with slightly longer recovery windows versus unconstrained global failover; the attached matrix compares RTO/RPO tradeoffs.

3) Backups & retention: Backups/snapshots are tenant-scoped and can be restricted to US-only storage buckets. Retention windows are configurable per-tenant and we support retention configuration plus ad-hoc legal hold and deletion APIs. We log backup creation events but backup contents are stored encrypted (KMS) in the pinned region.

4) Logging & PII: By default we capture request metadata (timestamps, model id, token counts, latency, route decisions) and request IDs for tracing. We do not persist request/response payloads by default unless a customer enables verbose tracing for diagnostics. For regulated customers we offer a PII-redaction mode where request/response payloads are never stored; only hash tokens and metadata are kept. We also provide a compliance export (audit log) that shows operational events without exposing user data.

Attachments included: cross-region-failover-matrix.xlsx (detailed RTO/RPO), redwood-region-pinning-ps.pdf (policy summary).

If helpful, I can prepare a short architecture diagram for your infra/security team showing control plane flow, KMS integration, and the enforcement check points.
